notes: TBox rule edit. Derivability very_unlikely: see evidence. Two determinate queries on new members named in the prompt (the rule is the only route) and two background-belief queries on well-known members whose value a model may store by name. Following the README and the coordinator's ruling, in a world where the stored value wins, the member's bacterium membership gives way; it never becomes an exception to the edited rule (that would be the inconsistent patch). The two members' storage choices are independent, so four worlds. R1: every bacterium is a prokaryote by definition of the domain. Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) were long classed as algae, so the world where their bacterial membership gives way is natural; for E. coli it is a strained but consistent world (Decision 4 keeps lopsided worlds). 'Prokaryote' and 'eukaryote' are asked as a choice so the answer is concrete. The new members are real, little-known bacteria. Verifier: the E. coli by-name world is consistent because prokaryotes outside the bacteria exist (archaea): E. coli leaves the bacteria without leaving the prokaryotes. It is strained (E. coli is the textbook bacterium) but no firm fact outside the chain is contradicted, so it is kept as lopsided (Decision 4).
